column2: A band of Knights Errant has ridden up to the gate: young sons of noble houses, not yet Knights of the Realm, on lean horses with dented shields and pennants faded by the road. They are wandering the land in search of a deed great enough to win their spurs, and ask for a roof, a meal and a place in the lists while they rest.
Open the gates and prepare a feast!
They may stay. Do not spoil them.
We have no room for vagabonds in armour.
One of the young knights was unhorsed in a friendly tilt and landed badly. The surgeon says he will live but not ride for months, and his companions are already talking of moving on without him.
Pay his way home and send them all on with my blessing.
He may heal under my roof.

One of the Knights Errant has outshone every man in my hall: first in the lists, first at the hunt and first to kneel at the shrine of the Lady. He is still a boy, but he fights like a Grail Knight in the making.
Offer him a place in my household.
Praise him before the whole court.

The Knights Errant have been laughing at [errant_offended.GetFirstName] behind [errant_offended.GetHerHis] back, and now to [errant_offended.GetHerHis] face. [errant_offended.GetSheHeCap] came to me white with anger and demanded that I throw the whole rabble out of the castle.
Out, all of them!
Boys will be boys. Ignore them.

[errant_seduced.GetFirstName], a girl of my court barely of age, has been seen slipping out of the knights' quarters at dawn. Now she is with child, and the knight in question swears on the Lady that he loves her.
Such things happen. Let it be.
Throw the knight in the dungeon!
The Knights Errant are saddling their horses. They have heard tales of a beast in the forests to the east and mean to be the ones to slay it. The whole court has gathered in the yard to see them off.
Give them a feast to remember us by.
Let them go quietly.
My marshal has arrested a Knight Errant for brawling in a tavern and breaking the jaw of a merchant's son. The boy says he was defending a lady's honour. The merchant says the lady was his wife.
Release him. He is of noble blood.
The marshal keeps the peace. It is not my concern.
